notes: Characters now know what happened before what. They could already see across conversations — in a group chat a character remembers their own private thread with you, and in a private chat they remember the groups they were in — but nothing ever said which came first, so a character reading both side by side had no way to tell whether the thing you told them alone happened before or after the group. Every message has always carried a timestamp, so the order was knowable; it simply was not being said. Each reply now begins with today's day and time, how long ago the last thing in this conversation was said, and a numbered running order of the conversations that character was part of, oldest first, ending with this one happening now — followed by the plain instruction that everything in those earlier conversations happened before this moment and should be treated as already said and already settled rather than as news to re-announce. The times themselves got more precise everywhere: 'thirty minutes ago' and 'three days ago' can be put in order, where the old 'in the last hour' and 'earlier today' could not. The privacy rule is unchanged and the running order obeys it — a character is only ever shown, or told about, conversations they were actually in, never someone else's private thread.
